speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) or a demyelinating disorder like tumefactive multiple sclerosis.

The sudden onset of right leg weakness and gait instability over one week, combined with a six-month history of progressive cognitive decline (forgetfulness, getting lost) and behavioral changes (paranoia, agitation), suggests a rapidly evolving neurological process affecting both the white matter of the brain and potentially the spinal cord. I need to see imaging to confirm the location and nature of the lesions.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast
REQUEST TEST: CSF_analysis_for_JC_virus_and_oligoclonal_bands
